rationale: The Latin anchor *mensa* refers to a physical table (a piece of furniture), and the contexts — brothers seated at the table (*sedentibus ad mensam fratribus*) and Psalm 22:5 (*parasti in conspectu meo mensam*, "thou preparest a table before me") — all point to a concrete piece of furniture. Table.n.02 ("a piece of furniture having a smooth flat top") is the best fit, though table.n.03 (a table set for a meal) is a close competitor; table.n.02 is preferred as the more basic, literal sense that underlies the attestations.
